ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL,
 BELGAUM, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR  COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF  COMPENSATION & ETC.

THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DA  JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435  MFA No. 100705 of 2015  HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 20.11.2014 passed in MVC no.2735/2012 by Principal Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal'), this appeal is filed.
2. Sri Vitthal S.Teli, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that on 28.04.2012 when claimant was working as a cleaner in vehicle bearing no.KA- 22/A-9388 returning from Machche after unloading goods, its driver drove it in rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against a motorcycle and thereafter against a tree.
As a result of accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to initially at Civil Hospital, Belagavi and thereafter at KLE Hospital, Belagavi.
He also took treatment at Kapileshwar Orthopedic Trauma and Surgical Care Center, Belagavi.

entities.text: Kapileshwar Orthopedic Trauma and Surgical Care Center, Belagavi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Despite treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability and consequent loss of earning capacity.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against owner and insurer of goods vehicle.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR 3.
Despite service, owner did not appear and was placed ex-parte.
Insurer appeared and opposed claim petition on all counts.

sentences.text: 2 4. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant examined himself and Dr.Prakash C.Wali as PWs1 and 2 and got marked Exhibits P1 to P17.

Respondent - Insurer examined its official as RW1 and got marked Exhibits R1 to R3.
5.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle by its driver, vehicle was insured and claimant was entitled for compensation from insurer as follows.
1

Medical and other incidental 65,000/-
expenses 2 Pain and suffering 5,000/-

3 Future loss of earning capacity due 2,07,360/-
to disability 4 Loss of income during laid up period 12,000/- 5 Loss of amenities in life 5,000/-
6 Removal of nails 15,000/-
 Total 3,09,360/-
 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR 6.
Dissatisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant was in appeal.
7. It was firstly submitted, claimant was 30 years of age working as cleaner in goods vehicle and earning 10,000/- per month.
Despite same, Tribunal erred in taking only 6,000/- per month as his income.
It was submitted, claimant sustained fractures of both femurs with implants, apart from fracture of 7th rib.
Despite same, Tribunal granted only 5,000/- towards pain and suffering which was grossly inadequate.
It was submitted, Tribunal awarded only 4,000/- towards diet and other incidental expenses.
Though claimant took inpatient treatment for a period of 46 days, Tribunal erred in considering only period of two months as layoff.
Even compensation awarded towards loss of amenities was on lower side and sought enhancement.
8. Further, since there were implants in both legs, he required surgery for removal.
Therefore, award of 15,000/- was inadequate and sought enhancement.

It was lastly submitted, PW2 - Dr.Prakash C.Wali, who had examined claimant and issued Ex.P10 - Disability Certificate had opined that there was permanent physical disability to extent of 55% on left leg and NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR 45% on right leg.
Such being case, Tribunal erred in taking only 18% as loss of earning capacity.

sentences.text: above grounds, sought for enhancement of compensation.
9. On other hand, Sri M.K.Soudagar, learned counsel for respondent opposed appeal.
It was submitted that Tribunal had considered material available on record while awarding compensation under each eligible head of compensation, leaving no scope for enhancement.
On said ground sought for rejection.

10. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
11.

From above and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement, point that would arise for consideration is:
'Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought?'
12.
Same is answered partly in affirmative for following reasons:
13. At outset, though claimant stated that he was earning 10,000/- per month as cleaner, same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, Tribunal was NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR justified in assessing it notionally.

But, notional income for year 2012 was 6,500/- and therefore,
Tribunal erred in considering it at 6,000/-.
14.

Indeed PW2 issued Ex.P10 - Disability Certificate stating assessing permanent physical disability to extent of 55% on left leg and 45% on right leg, but did not state whole body disability or loss of earning capacity.

15. Taking note of fact that claimant was working as cleaner in goods lorry and aged 30 years and extent of disability caused as well as fact that rods are inserted in both femur bones, assessment of loss of earning capacity at 18% by Tribunal would appear inadequate.
It is found appropriate to enhance it to 25%.

Thus, compensation towards future loss of income would require reassessment as follows:
6,500 x 25% x 12 x 16 = 3,12,000/-.
16.
Normally for fracture to a structural bone, this Court awards 40,000/- as compensation towards pain and suffering.
And in respect of other fractures, there is addition of 10,000/-.
Since claimant has sustained fracture of femur of both legs and NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR fracture of 7th rib, compensation towards pain and suffering is enhanced from 5,000/- to 90,000/-.
17. Claimant has produced medical bills for about 61,000/-.

Tribunal has awarded 65,000/-
towards medical and incidental expenses.

Since discharge summary produced would indicate total inpatient treatment for 46 days, award is confined to medical expenses and a separate sum of 35,000/- is awarded towards diet, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
Claimant sustained fracture of both femurs underwent surgery twice.

Instead of normal period of treatment/recuperation of 3 months, it is found appropriate to consider 4 months as period of Rupesh S/O Laxman Gavas vs Vijaykumar Gurulingappa Paramshetti on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120399838/
4 layoff.

sentences.text: At 6,500/- per month, claimant would be entitled for 26,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
In view of injuries and disability sustained, award of 5,000/- towards loss of amenities would be grossly inadequate and is enhanced to 40,000/-.
Normally 25,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses for removal of implants.
Since implants are there in both femurs, claimant would require to undergo surgery twice.
Therefore, NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR compensation towards same is enhanced to 50,000/-.

Thus, total reassessed compensation is :
 Loss of future income 3,12,000/-
 Pain and suffering 90,000/-
Medical expenses 65,000/-

Towards diet, conveyance and other 35,000/-
 incidental expenses

Loss of income during laid up period 26,000/-
 Loss of amenities 40,000/-
Future medical expenses 50,000/-

In view of above, following:
 ORDER  i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii. Claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,18,000/- as against Rs.3,09,690/- awarded by Tribunal.

Same shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
from date of petition till date of deposit.
iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3435 HC-KAR iv.
On deposit, entire amount is ordered to be released to claimant.
